long_biography.plain_text:
Román Sanahuja Pons entered the property business built by his father, Román Sanahuja Bosch, around affordable housing in Barcelona. As the second-generation leader, he broadened the family platform into market-rate homes, commercial centres, offices, industrial property and leisure developments, serving for many years as president of Sacresa.

At Metrovacesa, Sanahuja became a major shareholder and chairman during the family's push into Spain's listed property sector. Recent registry filings place him as president of Bahosa and a director of Indicesa L'Illa, alongside relatives from several family branches. These roles establish continuing stewardship, but company properties and historical shareholdings are kept separate from his current personal assets.

uncertainties.detail: Spanish regulatory and press sources use Román Sanahuja Pons, while Catalan coverage may use Romà. The Spanish accented Román form is accepted because it matches the immutable owner record and dominates authoritative filings.

Román Sanahuja Pons, born in 1939, is the father and predecessor of Román Sanahuja Escofet. CNMV documents name both men and their roles, preventing the son's education, directorships or executive work from being assigned to his father.

Sacresa projects, Bahosa assets, Indicesa L'Illa holdings and other group property belong to their respective companies. Family control and board membership do not make each portfolio asset Román Sanahuja Pons's direct personal property.

Historical CNMV disclosures documented substantial direct and indirect interests through personal holding companies. Those percentages are time-specific and are not carried forward as current ownership without a recent authoritative disclosure.

Sacresa and Metrovacesa leadership are historical. Official 2025 registry notices support current positions as Bahosa president and Indicesa L'Illa director, but those appointments alone do not establish current ownership percentages.

The owner record marks Sanahuja alive and gives a dated age in 2020. Current 2025 registry appointments support continued activity; only the independently repeated 1939 birth year is proposed, not an automatically changing present age.
No dedicated Forbes profile or identity-verified personal LinkedIn, Instagram or personal website was found. No social profile is proposed.
Business distress, litigation, corruption proceedings, private-family details beyond succession, and all private-vessel ownership, specifications and history were excluded from the biographies.
